prerequisites: It is recommended to have acquired the competencies of the Mathematics I course from the first year of the Degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Propose and solve mathematical exercises and problems graphically and in writing with the proper and rigorous terminology of mathematics applied to engineering.

syllabus_topics: Complex numbers and basic numerical calculation tools I: Equation solving; Functional approximation, interpolation; Numerical integration.
First-order ordinary differential equations. Separable and homogeneous differential equations; Exact differential equations; First-order linear and Bernoulli differential equations. Applications.
Second-order linear differential equations with constant coefficients. Method of variation of constants. Applications.
Basic numerical calculation tools II: Numerical methods in differential equations.

Integral transforms and application to solving differential equations: The Laplace transform and its properties; Inverse Laplace transform; Application of the Laplace transform to solving differential equations and systems of differential equations.
Fourier series and Fourier transform for solving differential equations. Applications.
Partial differential equations: Introduction to partial differential equations. Boundary conditions.
teaching_methods: Participative master class, conferences, company visits, fair attendance, etc.
Case resolution, role-playing, technique application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.
Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics (Laboratory).
Use of computational mathematical software (SageMath or wxMaxima).

assessment_methods.method: Resolution of short questions in groups in class
In-class group test exercises and in-class group mathematical problem-solving
Out-of-class group test exercises and out-of-class group mathematical problem-solving
In-class individual test exercises and in-class individual mathematical problem-solving
Oral presentation of exercises and/or integrated project
Integrated project of the first semester

assessment_rules: The course can be passed through continuous assessment, which requires a minimum of 80% class attendance. To pass, an average grade of 5.0 or higher is required, and an average grade of 4.0 or higher in each assessment instrument. If any instrument is graded below 4.0, a make-up in-person exam is required. In ordinary or extraordinary call exams, the final grade is 75% from a written test and 25% from the integrated project, requiring a grade higher than 5.0 to pass. If not enrolled in the Integrated Project course or without a grade for it, the qualification will be 100% of the exam grade or continuous assessment grade.
